tasks.behavior: A merchant profile has stores, and each of its invoices records one
acceptance: A merchant profile has stores with a name, a project ID, a default checkout close and up to 20 allowed https origins; its first store is made with it (a trigger), migration 58 backfills one per merchant profile with its return links' origins, and every merchant invoice records its store, which never changes

GET /v1/profiles/{profileId}/stores lists them (none for a personal or freelancer profile); PUT .../stores/{storeId} saves one by a browser-picked UUID, at most 20 per profile; another user 403, another profile's store 404 store_not_found, a personal or freelancer profile 409 not_merchant, a broken rule 422

Create takes storeId (default the first store; 422 on a non-merchant or unknown store), uses the store's default close without expiresIn, and refuses a merchant return link outside the store's allowed origins on create and when Edit changes it; owner reads return store {storeId, name}

The web app has a Stores page for merchant profiles to list, add and edit stores with a copyable project ID; New invoice picks the store when there are two or more and starts the close from its default; the invoice list and page name the store; axe finds 0 serious or critical violations
R-134, api.md, openapi.yaml, both architecture docs and DESIGN.md describe stores; required checks, backend-e2e and a11y-e2e pass
notes: 2026-10-24 review fail by reviewer: BLOCKING: apps/backend/internal/database/migrations/00058_stores.sql:31-32 backfill matches '^https://' case-sensitively before lower(), so an existing return_url like 'HTTPS://Shop.example.com/x' (accepted today: Go url.Parse lowercases the scheme, web isReturnLink uses URL.protocol) yields NULL, and array_agg keeps NULLs. allowed_origins then holds a NULL element; pgx cannot scan it into []string (verified: 'cannot scan NULL into *string'), so GET stores, every invoice create (profile.InvoiceStore) and returnUrl edits 500 for that merchant. Fix: substring(lower(i.return_url) FROM ...) and drop NULLs (FILTER (WHERE o IS NOT NULL)); add an upper-case-scheme row to TestStoresForExistingMerchants. NON-BLOCKING: (1) invoice/create.go:46 hashes a missing expiresIn as 3600, so for a merchant an omitted expiresIn (store default) and an explicit 3600 share a hash; a reused key with the other form replays instead of 409 (documented in api.md). (2) invoice/retainers.go:158 later months re-check returnUrl against the store's current origins; removing an origin makes every later month fail in the worker with only a log line. (3) new-invoice-form.tsx:352 maps a server 'allowed origins' 422 to the generic return-link error; edit-invoice.tsx:124 handles it. (4) new-invoice-form.tsx:120 expiryChoice falls back to 7 days for an API-set store default that is not a menu choice. (5) docs/PROJECT.md:186 R-134 sentence 'A store has a name...' is 26 words (D-84). (6) features/stores/tests/stores.test.ts tests the client mirror of a rule the server tests already guard; borderline under Which tests to keep. Checked OK: route auth (ProfileScoped + 403/401 tests), 404/409/422 paths, 20-store cap under profile lock, trigger, store-fixed trigger, FK (store_id, profile_id), view change (readers use named columns), Down migration, jobs/retainers/revise still create (revise carries storeId via restartFrom), features/stores imports no other feature, docs match code. Backend tests TestStores, TestMerchantInvoicesRecordTheirStore, TestStoresForExistingMerchants pass.

tasks.behavior: A store's logo and color brand its pay page
acceptance: The owner sets a store's logo and accent color; the pay page and the invoice PDF of that store's invoices show them, with contrast checked; where the logo is stored is decided with the owner first

tasks.behavior: A profile turns chains and tokens off, and a store narrows them
acceptance: A profile turns each enabled chain and token on or off, and a store can narrow that; payer-chooses invoices offer only what is left, a fixed invoice on a turned-off pair is 422, and invoices made earlier keep their options

lastWrapup.note: F289 implemented and independently reviewed; all seven verify checks passed. Wallet recovery, receipt backoff, shared header snapshots, independent chain jobs and shared weighted RPC budgets are ready for the approved PR to main and staging fast-forward. Invoice overlap and coherent header retries remain for money safety.
